answer: Primary cellular mechanism: p53-mediated DNA damage response driving apoptosis (programmed cell death). The combination treatment's differentially expressed genes (Cisplatin_IC50_CBD_IC50 vs DMSO; 1,582 DEGs at p<0.05, |log2FC|>0.5, baseMean>10, mapped to 1,485 unique symbols) are dominated by an up-regulated canonical p53/DNA-damage transcriptional program — CDKN1A(p21), DDB2, RRM2B, BTG2, ZMAT3, TIGAR, FDXR, BAX, FAS, PHLDA3, AEN, TP53INP1, STK17A, SUSD6, RPS27L, TNFRSF10C — biologically consistent with cisplatin-induced DNA damage potentiated by CBD culminating in apoptotic cell death; the pro-apoptotic arm (BAX, FAS) is up while the oxidative-stress/metabolic response genes move down. IMPORTANT CAVEAT: the gseapy.enrichr(Reactome_2022) call itself could NOT be executed in this environment — after exhaustive documented provisioning attempts (3× pip retries, alternate Enrichr/pypi hosts over http+https incl. amp.pharm.mssm.edu, alternate-DNS probe, full filesystem scan for wheels/GMTs/caches), the sandbox has no network and no gseapy/Reactome_2022 library. The named mechanism is therefore supported by the executed DE analysis plus evidence-based curated-set scoring (top ranked: p53/DNA damage response, up, 8/36 curated genes, hypergeometric p=4.6e-4 vs the 15,873-gene tested background), explicitly NOT by an actual Enrichr/Reactome_2022 run; results/enrichr_reactome2022 would finalize it exactly, using the saved one-command recipe and 1,485-symbol DEG list.
